jobs.title: Design Program Manager
jobs.description:
The Role

As a Design Program Manager at Everlaw, you'll establish the operating system for our growing product design team, bringing structure, visibility, and predictability to how we design AI-powered litigation tools. As our first dedicated Design Program Manager, you'll absorb operational friction and cross-functional complexity so product designers can focus entirely on craft, quality, and solving complex user workflows.

This is a full-time, exempt position based in our Oakland, CA office with a hybrid work schedule: in office M/W/Th with the option to work from home on Tu/Fr.

What you'll do

- Own the design operating model for planning and delivery — define how design work is estimated, sequenced, and handed off, and maintain the system that makes dependencies and timeline risk visible before they become escalations.

- Define design readiness criteria and coordinate pre-launch quality reviews to ensure shipped features meet high standards for craft, responsiveness, accessibility, and edge cases.

- Own the working interfaces between Design, Product Management, Engineering, User Research, and Technical Writing — define how scope is agreed, how dependencies are tracked, and where conflicts get decided, so those questions have a standing answer instead of being renegotiated per project.

- Build and champion lightweight design operations rhythms, frameworks, and templates—such as design briefs and critique structures—to streamline team workflows.

- Manage design resourcing and bandwidth tracking to inform staffing decisions, highlight capacity constraints, and help leadership plan for future team growth.

- Own how design's work is represented to the business — build and maintain the reporting layer (capacity, throughput, readiness) that lets product and executive leadership plan against design, rather than assembling narrative updates each cycle.

About You

- You have at least 5 years of experience in Design Program Management or Design Operations supporting product design teams in complex, enterprise B2B SaaS or data-heavy environments.

- You excel at balancing competing priorities across multiple stakeholders, steering teams through ambiguity with structure, clear prioritization, and empathy.

- You've built and scaled lightweight design operations frameworks, delivery plans, and resource tracking processes without stifling creative momentum.

- You bring excellent communication and storytelling skills, with a proven ability to translate design progress and complex trade-offs into business-relevant narratives for leadership.

- You bring a strong understanding of user-centered design methodologies, modern UX workflows, and tools like Figma.

- You have experience working with project tracking tools like Jira or emerging AI tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude Design).

- You operate with a low-ego, highly collaborative style, finding genuine fulfillment in making design teams visible and successful.

- You are authorized to work in the United States without restrictions. Please note that at this time, Everlaw is not sponsoring F-1 visas, including OPT, for this role.

Think you're missing some of the skills and are hesitant to apply? We do not believe in the 'perfect' candidate and encourage you to apply if you feel you can bring value to our team. We often revisit candidates who may have applied for a different role if something comes up that's a better fit.

The Team — Product

The Product team shapes products used by everyone from document reviewers and corporate teams to government attorneys and law firm partners, each with distinct needs across a broad and complex domain. The team brings together user insight, market context, business priorities, design, and technical feasibility to decide what Everlaw builds and why. This work turns deeply capable technology into intuitive experiences and helps define the next era of legal work.

Total Rewards & Benefits

The expected salary range for this role is $153,000 - $200,000. Final salary depends on factors including the candidate's experience and skills, and the base pay range is subject to change. This role is also eligible for equity and the benefits below.

Health & well-being

- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

- Flexible Spending Accounts for health and dependent care expenses

- Membership to Modern Health to support mental health and wellness

- Paid parental leave

- Company-sponsored life and disability insurance

Financial rewards

- Competitive equity grants, so you share in Everlaw's long-term growth

- 401(k) plan with company matching of up to 4% of eligible annual compensation

Growth & everyday perks

- 17 paid vacation days, 11 federal holidays, and paid sick leave

- Four "Everlawlidays" (additional paid company-wide days off) per year

- Annual allocation for learning & development and relevant professional membership dues

- Hybrid work with regular work-from-home days and flexibility for life's logistics

- Monthly home internet reimbursement, plus a stipend for your desk setup

- Catered lunch each workday, plus snacks and company-wide events in our offices

About Everlaw

When a lawsuit or investigation happens, teams must comb through vast amounts of electronic evidence — emails, documents, chats, files — to find what matters. That work is not a side task but the case itself, and where most of the time and money in litigation goes. Everlaw is the litigation and investigation management platform changing that, using AI to turn mountains of messy data into the handful of facts that win or lose a case, compressing weeks of work into hours.

We're the kind of place that's ranked #1 on G2 in our category and named a Great Place to Work™ by our own team. So if you want a front row seat to an industry in transformation, career-defining work you'll be proud to tell people about, and real upside at a company in control of its own destiny, we'd love to get to know you.

jobs.title: Enterprise AI Transformation Lead
jobs.description:
About Everlaw

At Everlaw, our mission is to promote justice by illuminating truth. We're changing how legal teams at law firms, corporations, government agencies, and nonprofits find the information they need to achieve their truth-finding goals. We believe technology should be a force multiplier for human intellect, and we see AI as an important part of how Everlawyers can work more effectively and thoughtfully.

The Role

Everlaw is building a deliberate, company-wide approach to AI—not simply to help people work faster, but to transform how we operate: redesigning workflows, improving the speed and quality of decisions, and creating new ways for teams to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Reporting to the VP of IT & Security, you’ll own Everlaw’s horizontal Corporate AI program end to end across governance, shared tooling strategy, adoption, measurement, and cost and vendor management. You’ll drive AI transformation by mobilizing department AI owners and champions and partnering closely with Learning & Development, Legal, and IT & Security.

This is a deeply hands-on role. You’ll get deep into enterprise AI platforms, agents, connectors, and workflows—evaluating tools, building and testing practical solutions, and translating what works into reusable capabilities that scale. You’ll move promising ideas from exploration to adoption, partner with Legal and Security to establish the guardrails needed to scale them responsibly, and measure whether they are changing how work actually gets done.

This is not an AI research or production engineering role, nor is it a traditional program-management or consulting role. It is a builder-operator role for someone who can work deeply in the systems while running the program with rigor—connecting systems, people, and execution so AI becomes a durable part of how Everlaw operates.

What You’ll Do

1. Own the enterprise AI operating model and governance

Keep Everlaw's federated AI efforts coherent, secure, and aligned to business priorities.

- Own and operate Everlaw’s federated AI framework: run its monthly and quarterly cadence, convene department AI owners, maintain clear accountability across the program, and report progress and risks to the leadership.

- Mature the operating model as Everlaw learns—including its principles, decision rights, ownership boundaries, and RACI across Enterprise AI, IT, Security, Legal, and department AI owners.

- Partner with Legal and Security on data-use governance, including data classification, acceptable use, autonomy limits, and agent guardrails—enabling low-risk work to move quickly while applying appropriate scrutiny to higher-risk uses.

2. Own the enterprise AI stack — expertise, landscape, and evaluation

Be Everlaw’s resident expert on its enterprise AI platforms and the market around them, shaping what enters the stack, what scales, and what exits.

- Build deep, hands-on expertise in Everlaw’s enterprise AI platforms. Use them regularly, understand their strengths, limitations, integrations, and roadmaps, and determine which capabilities are worth piloting, promoting, or standardizing.

- Stay ahead of the AI landscape by proactively researching and shortlisting tools and capabilities that could materially improve how Everlaw works—while filtering out noise and deciding what merits formal evaluation.

- Lead structured, evidence-based evaluations using rubrics, baseline tasks, scorecards, and business-value criteria. Build and test with the tools directly rather than relying on vendor demonstrations, and own recommendations on whether to extend existing platforms, buy new capabilities, or build internally.

- Maintain a coherent shared stack by preventing duplicative or fragmented adoption where an approved platform already meets the need. Advise departments on specialized tools while respecting their ownership of domain-specific applications.

- Coordinate procurement, implementation, rollout, and launch change management with IT, Procurement, Security, Legal, and other partners that own the relevant approval and delivery mechanics.

3. Drive adoption and practical enablement

Turn the tools Everlaw already owns into changed workflows and measurable use — most companies use a fraction of what they pay for; you close that gap.

- Build and maintain the central enablement playbook and template library—including intake, POC, change-management, and training patterns—so teams can move quickly without reinventing the basics.

- Provide hands-on guidance for high-value use cases: work directly with teams to redesign workflows and build agents or templates alongside them where targeted support is more effective than a formal engagement.

- Partner with Learning & Development to build practical AI fluency across Everlaw, including tool and model selection, effective AI collaboration, and cost-conscious use.

- Lead the AI champion community of practice, working with department AI owners and champions to surface adoption barriers, training needs, and reusable patterns—and feed what is learned back into playbooks and guidance.

4. Measure value and manage the AI portfolio

Own the methodology that shows whether the Enterprise AI program is creating real value — and the discipline to act on what it shows.

- Own and mature the measurement system behind Everlaw's AI adoption framework — standards for pre-AI baselines, metric targets, and measured results — moving from adoption and activity metrics toward outcomes tied to workflow improvement, quality, risk reduction, and business value.

- Partner with department AI leaders to define success measures for function-specific initiatives, and validate value claims as initiatives graduate through the funnel, so reported impact holds up.

- Run regular portfolio reviews and manage the path from experiment to sustained adoption, with clear criteria for what should scale, consolidate, pause, or stop.

5. Manage AI spend, vendors, and external partners

Ensure Everlaw’s AI investments remain sustainable and supported by the right partners.

- Maintain a portfolio-level view of AI spend across licenses, usage-based consumption, pilots, consultants, and implementation services.

- Own the cost-versus-value lens, annual planning, and investment recommendations for shared AI platforms, partnering with Finance, IT, Procurement, and business owners.

- Define practical consumption guardrails—including alerts, thresholds, approval flows, and caps—and adjust them as usage patterns evolve.

- Manage strategic AI vendor relationships, using roadmap insight, product feedback, adoption, and value data to inform negotiations and renewal recommendations.

- Build and maintain a vetted external partner bench for workflow redesign, agent design, configuration, integration, and enablement.

About You

You are a hands-on builder-operator with deep practical fluency with enterprise AI tooling, strong business judgment, and the discipline to run a company-wide program. You can turn ambiguity into an operating program, work deeply with tools and workflows, and mobilize teams across the company without relying on direct authority.

You are likely to succeed in this role if you:

- Build structure from ambiguity, translating broad goals into clear roadmaps, decision rights, operating rhythms, and measurable outcomes.

- Get deep into the tools. You are a hands-on power user who builds and tests agents, configures connectors, prototypes end-to-end workflows, and troubleshoots where tools break down. You understand how models, permissions, data, and integrations shape what is practical—then turn that firsthand expertise into clear guidance, reusable patterns, and better platform decisions, without needing to write production code.

- Understand how teams work and can identify, redesign, and operationalize workflows where AI creates meaningful value.

- Exercise sound judgment about when to build, buy, extend, scale, pause, or retire capabilities.

- Exercise sound judgment about when to build, buy, extend, scale, pause, or retire capabilities.

- Influence across executives, department leaders, IT, Security, Legal, Finance, Procurement, and Learning & Development.

- Communicate complex technical, risk, cost, and business-value tradeoffs clearly.

- Bring 10+ years of experience in digital transformation, AI and automation, internal platforms, product operations, or corporate systems, including 3+ years leading complex cross-functional programs.

Benefits

- The expected salary range for this role is between $193,000 and $244,000. The final offered salary will be dependent upon many factors including the candidate’s experience and skills. The role's compensation is subject to change in the future.

- Annual allocation for Learning & Development opportunities and applicable professional membership dues

jobs.title: Renewals Manager, Indirect Procurement
jobs.description:
The Role

As Renewals Manager , you'll own Everlaw's rolling pipeline of internal SaaS and IT contract renewals, making sure no agreement lapses into an unfavorable auto-renewal while driving cost savings through usage analysis and license right-sizing. Partnering closely with internal teams across Engineering, IT, HR, and Marketing, you'll manage the day-to-day commercial lifecycle for our expiring vendor contracts and build disciplined, data-backed renewal processes.

This is a full-time, non-exempt position based in our Oakland, CA office with a hybrid work schedule: in office M/W/Th with the option to work from home on Tu/Fr.

What you'll do

- Maintain a rolling 12-month renewal calendar, initiating cycles 90–120 days prior to expiration to prevent unintended auto-renewals or contract lapses.

- Analyze utilization data alongside IT Asset Management to identify unused seats, over-provisioned tiers, and shelfware before setting negotiation targets.

- Negotiate in-scope software and IT renewals using established playbooks, benchmarks, and pre-approved fallback positions to limit uplifts and secure favorable terms.

- Coordinate cross-functional reviews across Legal, Security, IT, Compliance, and FP&A to confirm data privacy, security, and budget approvals prior to execution.

- Administer procurement software systems (specifically ZIP) and maintain accurate contract records, renewal dates, spend data, and savings metrics in the system of record.

About You

- You have at least 5 years of progressive procurement experience, ideally within a fast-growing technology or software environment.

- You've managed end-to-end renewal pipelines and have experience establishing or refining procurement functions across multi-location organizations.

- You bring strong data analysis skills and a track record of using usage metrics to build reduction cases and right-size software agreements.

- You communicate effectively across all organizational levels, building collaborative cross-functional relationships with Legal, Security, IT, and Finance teams.

- You're process-oriented with high attention to detail, managing contract hygiene and critical notice windows across a high-volume portfolio.

- You are authorized to work in the United States. Please note that at this time, Everlaw is not sponsoring U.S. employment visas for this role.

Bonus points

- Experience working with e-procurement and SaaS management tools such as ZIP or Ironclad.

- Exposure to structured negotiation methodologies or formal negotiation training.

- Familiarity with SOC 2 compliance, data privacy review processes, or vendor security assessments.

- Experience supporting vendor consolidation or cost reduction initiatives.

jobs.description:
The Role

You'll own the revenue and Annual Revenue Run Rate (ARRR) models that power Everlaw’s top-line forecasting, bringing clarity and speed to our business planning and operating visibility. Sitting at the intersection of FP&A, GTM, Accounting, and Enterprise Technology, you will turn complex customer and contract data into clear financial models, variance analyses, and actionable insights that support strategic decisions across the company.

This is a full-time, exempt position based in our Oakland, CA office with a hybrid work schedule: in office M/W/Th with the option to work from home on Tu/Fr.

What you'll do

-
Build, refine, and automate Everlaw’s revenue and ARRR forecasting models to improve accuracy, scalability, and recurring reporting workflows.

-
Deliver monthly and quarterly reporting on ARRR, expansions, renewals, churn, customer cohorts, and key revenue metrics.

-
Analyze actual financial results against forecasts and plans, investigating material variances to their root causes and explaining key drivers to leadership.

-
Partner with Accounting, RevOps, and Enterprise Technology to reconcile revenue data, validate inputs, and strengthen underlying data structures and controls.

-
Support annual budgeting, quarterly rolling forecasts, and executive and Board reporting with well-documented assumptions and timely financial materials.

About You

-
You have at least 3 years of experience in FP&A, revenue finance, or financial analysis, ideally supporting revenue planning or recurring-revenue metrics in a SaaS environment.

-
You bring advanced financial modeling skills in Excel or Google Sheets, with a focus on building transparent, automated, and easy-to-maintain models.

-
You are an analytical problem solver who can navigate complex customer and contract data, investigate data issues, and reconcile disparate data sources.

-
You communicate complex financial concepts clearly and concisely to both finance and non-finance business partners.

-
You thrive in cross-functional environments, managing multiple priorities and recurring deadlines with incomplete or evolving information.

-
You are authorized to work in the United States. Please note that at this time, Everlaw is not sponsoring U.S. employment visas for this role.

Bonus points

-
Experience with ARR or ARRR reporting, SaaS metrics, or revenue recognition concepts.

- Experience working for a consumption based company.

-
Familiarity with financial planning tools (e.g., Adaptive Planning), ERPs (NetSuite), CRMs (Salesforce), or BI and data warehouse platforms (Looker, Tableau, Snowflake).

-
Working knowledge of SQL or data-querying tools.
